sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Component-modeled vintage three-head tape echo with a three-spring reverb tank. Port of Tape Echo 2 by Dusk Audio (GPL-3.0). The record EQ and tape saturation sit INSIDE the feedback loop, so each repeat darkens and compresses instead of just getting quieter — which is what lets high Intensity settings bloom into warm, stable self-oscillation.

sections.heading: Mode
sections.body: Which of the three playback heads are live, and whether the spring tank is in circuit. Digits are the heads, R is reverb: H1, H2, H3, H2+3, H1+R, H2+R, H3+R, H12+R, H23+R, H13+R, H123R, Rev. Head 1 is the shortest tap, head 3 the longest (about 1.00 / 1.91 / 2.76 times the motor time). Rev is spring only, no tape.

sections.heading: Repeat Rate
sections.body: Capstan motor speed, and so the delay time. Left is slow (about 177 ms on head 1), right is fast (about 69 ms). Heads 2 and 3 scale up from that. Changes glide like a real transport rather than jumping, because the motor has inertia.

sections.heading: Intensity
sections.body: Feedback — how much of the playback head sum is fed back onto the tape. Above roughly three quarters it self-oscillates and builds into a growing drone. That is the hardware behaviour, and it gets loud: ride Echo Volume.

sections.heading: Echo Volume
sections.body: Level of the tape echo path in the output mix. Independent of Reverb Volume, so you can run either alone.

sections.heading: Reverb Volume
sections.body: Level of the spring tank. Only audible in the modes that include R. The tank is three bidirectional dispersive springs, so an impulse arrives as an ascending chirp and each round trip gets darker and more smeared.

sections.heading: Mix
sections.body: Dry against the combined wet bus. 50 percent is the classic parallel setting with both paths at unity — below that the dry stays at unity while the wet fades in, above it the wet stays at unity while the dry fades out. 0 is fully dry, 100 fully wet.

sections.heading: Tempo Sync
sections.body: Locks the leading active head to the host tempo instead of the Repeat Rate knob. The note comes from the Echo Rate Note detent, read through whichever head is leading in the current Mode.

sections.heading: Echo Rate Note
sections.body: The eleven physical tempo-sync detents, 1 (longest) to 11 (shortest). The same detent means a different note depending on the leading head, exactly as on the hardware — changing Mode keeps the detent and reassigns its note. Notes the transport cannot physically reach are pinned at the motor limit rather than transposed.

sections.heading: Input Drive
sections.body: Preamp gain into the record stage. Higher settings push the tape into saturation and soft compression before anything is recorded, thickening the repeats.

sections.heading: Bass
sections.body: Low shelf on the echo path only, about plus or minus 17 dB. The dry signal is untouched. Cutting bass keeps long feedback washes from turning muddy.

sections.heading: Treble
sections.body: High shelf on the echo path only, about plus or minus 17 dB. Because it is inside the loop, cutting treble makes each successive repeat darker than the last.

sections.heading: Wow & Flutter
sections.body: Transport instability: slow wow, capstan flutter, and a stochastic scrape band around 6 Hz. Zero is not perfectly still — the modeled transport always has some motion, matching the reference machine.

sections.heading: Tape Age
sections.body: Cartridge condition. New is a fresh tape and serviced transport. Used and Old progressively add noise, more wow, high-frequency loss, level wobble and splice wear.

sections.heading: Input Send
sections.body: The dub switch. Off stops feeding new audio onto the tape while the existing repeats keep circulating and decaying, and the spring stays live. Play a phrase, switch it off, and the echoes wash out on their own over a clean dry signal.

sections.heading: Credits
sections.body: DSP: Tape Echo 2 by Dusk Audio, github.com/dusk-audio/dusk-audio-plugins, GPL-3.0. The DSP core is vendored unmodified. Move port by athousanddetails.
